source_excerpts.text:
3. The complete service cycle

The ready state contains copper on the counterelectrode, measured bath concentration, clean separated terminals and no useful copper bridges.

Conditional time allocation
Stage	Included operations	Allocated time
Engage and qualify	Docking, alignment, clamping, filling, deposition, draining, rinsing, drying and proof	99.1 s
Release	Capture and verify unloading, reconnect, strip, rinse, dry, force-limited separation	94.6 s
Restore	Recover fluid, restore stock, inspect, remove added water and check readiness	55.0 s

These are complete budgets under introduced assumptions. They are not predictions that a mechanically sound seam has formed.

During installation, an approximately 1 kN external clamp acts against retractable fixture stops. It must react fluid pressure without forcing each island into an uncontrolled contact state. The stops and support are removed before the useful hold.

The proposed routine acceptance proof is 1.15 times the reference load endpoints, with orientation coverage calibrated against the complete assembly. A 20-second proof budget is allocated, but its ability to reject hidden weak seams is unestablished.

Before release, the support takes the useful load. The release actuator commands no more than 15 N at a central port and stops at 20 N. The interface is drained, rinsed, vented and dried before separation: a remaining liquid meniscus can otherwise produce a substantial separation force.

The robot is allocated 110 seconds of occupied time across the approximately 249-second active sequence. This requires real interleaving: the paid cart and passive fixture retain the parts while the robot performs other paid work. If the robot simply waits, its entire waiting period must be charged.
